additional_info.subject: RE: ID0367898-DC/Si-D/SE [MP / P6 170000700] Missing Converters in DC1 CRM:00643000784
additional_info.body:
Hi Magnus,
Greetings of the day!
In relation to this power converter issue, we have checked with the help of Debug station and it seems there is an issue with power converter. Please follow the below steps for troubleshooting.
1. Checked the converter grouping in the SCB, it looks fine as per the Flex configuration.
2. Please check if the power converter are properly connection to its shelf case.
3. Check for any loose connection of any power cable or CAN communication cables of the converter and measured the voltage across it with the help of multimeter. Check the resistance across CAN communication cables.
4. Please see to the display of the power converter whether it is OFF state or ON?
5. Try swapping the power converter with the good one and if the error flag was changed to the replaced one then we can suspect that the converter is faulty.
6. If all the steps are performed and you still see the power converter are faulty, we suggest you to replace it as we can't rework to it.

A couple of questions.
Point 3. How do you measure the voltage on the converters in a safe way and where do you want us to measure the resistance of the canbus?

additional_info.subject: RE: Sv: ID0367898-DC/Si-D/SE [MP / P6 170000700] Missing Converters in DC1 CRM:00643000784
additional_info.body:
Hi Magnus,
Please find my responses to the below points.
Point 3. How do you measure the voltage on the converters in a safe way and where do you want us to measure the resistance of the canbus?
Y
ou can measure the voltage safely by taking the necessary precautions and following the five safety rules. You can measure the resistance on the power converter pins 7 and 8, which are CANBH and CANBL, respectively
.
Point 4. How do think that we can see the display? It’s all the way in and in the bottom? You have to remember that there is no power on the converters when the doors open and we then need to disable this function to get power.
You can troubleshoot this action by using a cable tie on the door switch and making sure you're taking safety precautions, as the charger will be live. Try pulling out one of the power converters to see the display of the others that are at the back.
Point 5. Why do you think that this will help?
This will help in clearly identifying that the power converter is faulty. When you replace the converter with a healthy one, the error flag on the SCB will change. For example, it may indicate 'Missing converter in DC1 to DC2'.
They have been working for quite a long time so why do you suspect that there is something else wrong then the converter?
We can't comment on the converter as there are many power electronics components and circuits inside the power converter that we're not allowed to troubleshoot.
I have had similar issues before and never found anything else wrong then the converter itself.
Y
es, as we can check the power cables and CAN communication cables, but the power converter is still not powering up, we recommend replacing it
Thank you.
With best regards,
eMobility Tech Support Team -
Shrey

additional_info.subject: RE: Sv: ID0367898-DC/Si-D/SE [MP / P6 170000700] Missing Converters in DC1 CRM:00643000784
additional_info.body:
Hi Magnus,
I hope this email finds you well.
To answer your question, no, this is not related to the firmware. However, for point number 3, you can check the resistance in the wires for CANBH and CANBL without any power.
For point number 4, you can pull out the converter on the opposite side of the damaged one while the charger is powered off. After that, power it on and check whether the display shows anything or if it’s completely black.
Regarding the converter issue you're seeing in other chargers, have you created a ticket for it? If not, please do so, and we'll be happy to assist you.
Thank you for your patience and understanding.
Best Regards,
Shrey Sharma
